name: GGUF IQ2_XXS (2.0625 bpw, almost-true 2-bit with a 16-bit scale per 256)
bits: 2.3824 measured avg (llama.cpp quantize README, Llama-3.1-8B); official tool string '2.06 bpw quantization'. block_iq2_xxs = { ggml_half d; uint16_t qs[QK_K/8]; } = 2 + 64 = 66 bytes / 256 = 2.0625 bpw
quality_delta: Official tool string '2.06 bpw quantization' (qlab2-quantize-options-table); no controlled fp16 delta published. Null + note.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-10-04: was 256 -> still 256, but now with a basis instead of a coincidence. iq2_xxs has NO sub-block scale plane: block_iq2_xxs is `{ ggml_half d; uint16_t qs[QK_K/8]; }` = 64 bytes of 2-bit indices plus a single fp16 for all 256 values, which is exactly why the header comment says it 'ends up using 2.0625 bpw because of the 16-bit scale for each block of 256'. Here the super-block size and the scale group DO coincide at 256. Contrast iq2_s/iq2_xs, which add sub-block scales at 32. SCHEMA MISMATCH: there is no ggml/iq* value in the quantization scheme enum, so this record uses the closest existing value 'gguf-q4_k_m' (or 'gguf-q2_k') and puts the true type in `name` and `bits`. Requested enum additions are listed in the task report. Weight-only by construction: activations are promoted to q8_K (an intermediate dot-product format, not a storage format) and the matmul runs at fp16/bf16, so native_support is deliberately EMPTY and the whole accelerator ecosystem is emulated_support. No accelerator has an i-quant or k-quant path in silicon. COMMON TO ALL IQ-QUANTS, verified from ggml/src/ggml-common.h: they use the QK_K = 256 super-block like the K-quants, but instead of a UNIFORM integer grid they quantize to indices into a per-block CODEBOOK of 256 learned non-uniform 4-bit values (the 'i' in i-quant is for the codebook grid / i-quant from the ik_llama.cpp lineage). The index lookup is table-driven at dequant time, which is why they compress better than K-quants at the same nominal bits and why they dequantize more slowly - the dot product needs a gather from the codebook. This is a real throughput trade, not a free win. BACKEND SITUATION, verified: the CUDA library shipped in llamafile releases is size-optimized and OMITS the IQ-quant kernels (IQ1_*, IQ2_*, IQ3_*, IQ4_*); offloading an IQ-quantized model to an NVIDIA GPU therefore leaves those layers on the CPU with correct output but no GPU acceleration (qlab2-llamafile-support-docs). The Metal and ROCm builds are NOT size-optimized and include full IQ-quant GPU support - so an RX 7900 XTX on ROCm/HIP is in a materially better IQ position than an RTX 4090 on a stock llamafile build. Vulkan has no dedicated IQ-quant path. Upstream llama.cpp has per-type dequant kernels; ik_llama.cpp additionally ships the Trellis family (IQ1_KT/IQ2_KT/IQ3_KT/IQ4_KT, integer-base trellis, CUDA PR 113 / Metal PR 475 / NEON PR 471 / CPU PR 441) and _R4/_R16 row-interleaved variants. IQ2_XXS is the simplest i-quant and the header comment explains its cost precisely: '(Almost) "true" 2-bit quantization. Due to the need to use blocks as per ggml design, it ends up using 2.0625 bpw because of the 16-bit scale for each block of 256.' Structurally it is qs[QK_K/8] = 32 uint16 values = 64 bytes of 2-bit codebook indices plus a single fp16 d - there is no sub-block scale plane at all, unlike iq2_xs/iq2_s. That absence is exactly why it is the fastest 2-bit i-quant to dequantize and also why it is the weakest (one scale for 256 values). The 'XXS' naming convention across i-quants is 'extra extra small' = smallest size in the family. llama-quant.cpp maps LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_IQ2_XXS directly to GGML_TYPE_IQ2_XXS, and IQ2_XXS is also the promotion target for 8-expert (Mixtral) models when IQ1_S/IQ1_M is requested - 'if (n_expert == 8) { if IQ1_S or IQ1_M -> IQ2_XXS }', an explicit statement that Mixtral's experts do not tolerate 1-bit. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'gguf-q2_k' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'gguf-iq2-xxs'. 
NATIVE_SUPPORT CLASSIFIED 2026-10-04: this field is still [] and that is CORRECT, but the empty list used to be ambiguous between three different states and now is not. Reason class on this record: LLAMA.CPP INTEGER STORAGE TYPE, SO STRUCTURALLY ABSENT. Every GGUF type here is a packed integer block format read by a dequant kernel (dequantize_row_*) and then executed as FP16; ggml publishes no int4 or sub-8-bit tensor-core path that consumes these blocks directly. The llama.cpp CUDA and Vulkan backends both run these formats by dequantizing. Consequence for a reader: nothing further to verify - and note the contrast with nvfp4/mxfp4/mxfp8 in this repo, which ARE hardware formats on Blackwell and carry populated native_support lists, so '4-bit' alone does not predict this field. The full statement of the three-way distinction, and the worked list of all 72 empty records by class, is in gotcha quant-native-support-empty-means-three-different-things. Rule of thumb for this field everywhere in the repo: if the bits field carries an 'a16', or the scheme is KV-cache-only or a llama.cpp integer storage type, an empty native_support is a DEFINITION and needs no verification; only a W4A4/W8A8/sub-8-bit format with research kernels can have an empty list that is a real finding.
